title: Launch Trajectory Scorecard and Readiness Tracker
content:
Purpose:
A compact, single-sheet view to run weekly readiness check-ins for upcoming product rollouts. Combines a small KPI scoreboard (health signals), a time-phased runway of critical milestones, and a deterministic launch-gate checklist with explicit pass/fail triggers and mitigations. Designed to be used by Product Ops + Launch Owner during cross-functional readiness calls (Mon/Wed).

Quick summary guidance:
- Use the color bands per metric to drive gating decisions (Green = go, Yellow = monitor + contingency ready, Red = block).
- If any gating item is Red at the final canary gate (72h before wide release), escalate to the RTE and delay deploy window.
- Owners must update the sheet daily during final week.

1) Scoreboard (weekly snapshot - fields):
Metric | Owner | Target | Current (last 24h) | Band | Trend | Action if Yellow/Red
- End-to-end latency p50 (ms) | SRE/Infra | <=120ms | 142ms | Yellow | ↑ | Enable burst pool + reduce batch size; throttle non-critical routes
- Token cost per 1k | Product Ops | <=$1.40 | $1.35 | Green | ↓ | N/A
- Error rate (5xx % of requests) | Serving Runtime | <=0.5% | 0.8% | Red | ↑ | Revert last kernel tweak (SR-235) + route to fallback model variant
- Regression rate on key eval set (NLP-R1) | Applied ML | <=1.0% | 1.3% | Yellow | ↔ | Rollback quant config or quarantine prompt subset
- Canary satisfaction (NPS-like probe) | Solutions Eng | >=80% | 77% | Yellow | ↓ | Pause expansion and run triage with CS
- Observability retention (events/day) | Observability | >=99% | 99.6% | Green | ↔ | N/A
- Capacity headroom (% free GPU seats) | Dedicated Ops | >=20% | 15% | Yellow | ↓ | Activate burst pool, limit background batch jobs

Notes on scoreboard interpretation:
- Band thresholds are configurable per product; defaults above are conservative for high-risk features (latency-sensitive).
- 'Trend' is qualitative (↑, ↓, ↔) over the last 72h.
- 'Action' must be a discrete, executable mitigation with owner and PR/Runbook link.

2) Time-phased runway (14-day view)
Columns: Day-14 .. Day-0 (release) with milestone rows. Example rows:
- Feature freeze: Day-10 (owner: Eng-Feature) - status: complete
- Canary window start: Day-6 (owner: Release Eng) - status: in_progress
- Canary capacity target: Day-5 (owner: Dedicated Ops) - status: partial
- Eval passes (quality gates): Day-4 (owner: Applied ML) - status: pending
- Ops playbook ready: Day-3 (owner: SRE) - status: pending
- Final canary (72h check): Day-3 - status: pending
- Pre-switchover validation: Day-1 - status: pending
- Rollwide: Day-0 - status: pending

Runway comments:
- If capacity < target at Day-6, re-evaluate traffic ramp schedule and announce delay window immediately.
- Keep a short list of rollback commits and an automated revert job (gh action) referenced in the playbook.

3) Launch-gate checklist (deterministic pass/fail)
Each gate item: owner | pass condition | evidence required | fail action
- Observability hooks installed | Observability | All required metrics emitting to the dashboard and alerting rules tested | Fail -> Block release; remediate with obs pager runbook
- Rate-limit and quota policy in prod | Security/Platform | Policies deployed and smoke-tested under load | Fail -> Delay; apply temporary quota and schedule hotfix
- Canary quality regression | Applied ML | No >1.0% regression against primary eval set for 72h | Fail -> Quarantine model variant; fall back to prior model
- End-to-end latency SLO | SRE | p50 <= target and p95 within SLO for 24h | Fail -> Shift traffic away from baseline model; enable small-batch mode
- Cost safety net | Finance/Product Ops | Projected token cost within committed budget at 2x expected traffic | Fail -> Enable throttling on non-critical routes; require exec approval for overspend
- Customer-facing docs & KB | Solutions Eng | KB published and copy reviewed; support playbook attached | Fail -> Hold release; publish stub KB and route support to internal channel

4) Contingency playbook (short actions tied to scoreboard triggers)
- If Error rate >0.6% for 2 consecutive hours: immediate triage, route 20% of traffic to fallback model, notify SRE and Applied ML, open incident CRIT-1
- If Canary satisfaction drops below 70%: pause expansion, capture 100 sample conversations, label for root-cause, and roll back last UX prompt change
- Latency p95 blowout: automatically reduce max_seq for background batches and disable prefix caching for non-hot routes

5) Decision matrix for go/no-go (final canary gate 72h before)
- All Red metrics -> NO GO (must fix and re-evaluate)
- Any critical checklist item Fail -> NO GO
- <=2 Yellow items with concrete mitigations and owners -> CONDITIONAL GO (stage-limited rollout + increased monitoring)
- All Green or trivial Yellows -> GO

6) Communication and cadence
- Weekly readiness call: Mon 09:30 PT (15m sync) - owners update scoreboard and runway; product ops chairs
- Final canary review: 72h before release - 60m deep-dive with SRE, Applied ML, Release Eng, Solutions Eng, Finance
- Post-launch health check: Day+1 and Day+7 (15m each)

7) Example row from the sheet (operational sample)
- Metric: Error rate 5xx | Owner: Serving Runtime | Target: <=0.5% | Current: 0.8% | Band: Red | Trend: ↑ | Action: Revert SR-235 (PR #2934), route 30% to fallback model variant v1.24, open incident PROD-521

8) Short checklist for owners before each runway update:
- Confirm linked runbooks and PRs are attached to metric actions
- Validate that evidence links (dashboards, logs, PRs) are reachable and not behind private links
- Mark items with ETA and assign a single owner for each mitigation

Appendix: useful links and ownership map
- Launch playbook (canonical): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PROD/launch-playbook-2026-Q1
- Rollout orchestration repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rollouts
- Incident runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/incident-handling

Next steps (for this draft):
- Product Ops to run one dry-run using the sheet on 2026-03-12 and capture friction points
- SRE to confirm alert thresholds and test smoke alerts by 2026-03-15
- Applied ML to provision evaluation run by 2026-03-16 and report trend

Comments and outstanding questions:
- Can we add a small automated step that snapshots metric evidence links into the sheet at each update? (Marco)
- Finance: need a short definition of "token cost projection" used above to make cost gating consistent across teams. (Samantha)

End of sheet text.
